source_text: Καὶ ὑμῦς οὖν ἀξιοῦμεν ὑπογράψαντας τὸ ὑμῖν δοκοῦν προθεῖναι τουτὶ τὸ βιβλίδιον, ὅπως καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις τὰ ἡμέτερα γνωσθῇ καὶ δύνωνται της ψευδοδοξίας καὶ ἀγνοίας τῶν καλῶν ἀπαλλαγῆναι, οἳ παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν αἰτίαν ὑπεύθυνοι ταῖς τιμωρίαις γίνονται [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα], διὰ τὸ ἐν τῇ φύσει τῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἶναι τὸ γνωριστικὸν καλοῦ καὶ αἰσχροῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ ἡμῶν, οὓς οὐκ ἐπίστανται τοιαῦτα ὁποῖα λέγουσιν αἰσχρὰ πράττειν, καταψηφίζεσθαι, καὶ διὰ τὸ χαίρειν τοιαῦτα πράξασι θεοῖς καὶ ἔτι νῦν ἀπαιτοῦσι παρὰ ἀνθρώπων τὰ ὅμοια, ὡς ἐκ τοῦ καὶ ἡμῖν, ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι, θάνατον ἢ δεσμὰ ἢ ἄλλο τι τοιοῦτον προστιμᾶν ἑαυτοὺς κατακρίνειν, ὡς μὴ δέεσθαι ἄλλων δικαστῶν.
orientation: Justin, having explained that Christians possess the whole truth through the Word, now asks the Roman authorities to publish his written defense so others may learn the truth and be freed from false opinion.
pass_a_gloss: And you therefore we ask, having subscribed what seems good to you, to publish this little book, so that also to the others our things may be known and they may be able from false opinion and ignorance of good things to be freed, who by their own fault liable to punishments become [so that these things may be known to humans], because in the nature of humans is the ability to know good and shameful, and because they condemn us, whom they do not know to do such shameful things as they say, and because they rejoice in gods who did such things and still now demand from humans the same things, so that from this also against us, as doing such things, death or bonds or some other such thing they impose, condemning themselves, so that they need no other judges.

choices.english: having subscribed what seems good to you
choices.why: Keeps the technical sense of official endorsement by writing beneath, which fits the request to the Roman authorities to approve and publish.
rejected: having signed off on your opinion

choices.why: προθεῖναι means to set forth publicly; βιβλίδιον is a diminutive, so 'little book' preserves the modest tone.
rejected: to set before you this booklet

choices.why: The compound means false opinion or false belief; 'false opinion' is the most literal rendering and matches the philosophical context.

choices.english: the ability to know good and shameful
choices.why: γνωριστικόν is a substantive adjective meaning the faculty of knowing; 'ability to know' renders it clearly.
rejected: the knowledge of good and shameful
the discernment of good and shameful

choices.why: The verb means to impose an additional penalty; 'impose as penalty' captures the judicial force.

choices.english: so that they need no other judges
choices.why: The result clause with ὡς plus infinitive is rendered literally; the point is that by condemning Christians they condemn themselves.
rejected: so as not to require other judges

pass_b_english: We ask you, then, to endorse what seems right to you and publish this little book, so that others may also learn what we teach and be freed from false opinion and ignorance of what is good. These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, so that these things may be known to all people, because the ability to know good and shameful is part of human nature, and because they condemn us—whom they do not know to be guilty of the shameful acts they allege—and because they delight in gods who have done such things and still now demand the same from human beings. For by imposing death or imprisonment or some other such penalty on us, as though we did such things, they condemn themselves, needing no other judges.
notes: The bracketed phrase [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα] appears to be a marginal gloss or duplicate that interrupts the syntax; it is included in the source but may be an interpolation.

problems.quote: These people become liable to punishment through no fault of their own
problems.source_quote: οἳ παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν αἰτίαν ὑπεύθυνοι ταῖς τιμωρίαις γίνονται [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα], διὰ τὸ ἐν τῇ φύσει τῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἶναι τὸ γνωριστικὸν καλοῦ καὶ αἰσχροῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ ἡμῶν, οὓς οὐκ ἐπίστανται τοιαῦτα ὁποῖα λέγουσιν αἰσχρὰ πράττειν, καταψηφίζεσθαι, καὶ διὰ τὸ χαίρειν τοιαῦτα πράξασι θεοῖς καὶ ἔτι νῦν ἀπαιτοῦσι παρὰ ἀνθρώπων τὰ ὅμοια, ὡς ἐκ τοῦ καὶ ἡμῖν, ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι, θάνατον ἢ δεσμὰ ἢ ἄλλο τι τοιοῦτον προστιμᾶν ἑαυτοὺς κατακρίνειν, ὡς μὴ δέεσθαι ἄλλων δικαστῶν
problems.why: The bracketed phrase [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα] is omitted entirely.
problems.fix: add: 'that these things may be known to all people' or similar after 'their own'.

problems.quote: through no fault of their own
problems.why: παρὰ τὴν αἰτίαν means 'contrary to their own fault/cause,' i.e., 'through their own fault,' not 'through no fault.'
problems.fix: 'through their own fault' or 'being themselves at fault'
problems.ruling: παρὰ τὴν αἰτίαν means 'contrary to their own fault' = through their own fault, opposite of 'through no fault.'

problems.quote: by imposing death or imprisonment or some other such penalty on us as if we did these things, they condemn themselves
problems.source_quote: ὡς ἐκ τοῦ καὶ ἡμῖν, ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι, θάνατον ἢ δεσμὰ ἢ ἄλλο τι τοιοῦτον προστιμᾶν ἑαυτοὺς κατακρίνειν
problems.why: ὡς ἐκ τοῦ means 'with the result that from this' or 'so that by this,' not 'as a result, by imposing.' The structure is result clause: 'so that by imposing... they condemn themselves.' But 'as if we did these things' misrepresents ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι—this is concessive/causal 'since we do such things' (the alleged acts), not counterfactual 'as if.'
problems.fix: 'so that by imposing death or imprisonment on us, since they claim we do such things, they condemn themselves'
problems.ruling: ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι is causal 'since we do such things,' not counterfactual 'as if we did'; the punishers believe Christians actually do them.

edits.old: These people become liable to punishment through no fault of their own, because
edits.new: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, so that these things may be known to all people, because

edits.old: As a result, by imposing death or imprisonment or some other such penalty on us as if we did these things, they condemn themselves
edits.new: So that by imposing death or imprisonment or some other such penalty on us, since they claim we do such things, they condemn themselves

fixed: The bracketed phrase is now included in the English.
The phrase 'through no fault of their own' has been corrected to 'through their own fault'.
The result clause and the concessive/causal force of 'ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι' have been corrected.

problems.quote: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, so that these things may be known to all people
problems.source_quote: οἳ παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν αἰτίαν ὑπεύθυνοι ταῖς τιμωρίαις γίνονται [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα]
problems.why: Bracketed text is editorial; but even without it, 'so that these things may be known' misrepresents the causal logic. The Greek says they become liable 'through their own fault' (παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν αἰτίαν), and the bracketed εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι is purpose/result of their liability, not of Justin's request. The English makes 'so that these things may be known' follow from Justin's request to publish, when in Greek it explains why they are liable.
problems.fix: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, [that these things may be known to people], because...

edits.old: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, so that these things may be known to all people, because
edits.new: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault—that these things may be known to all people—because

fixed: The causal logic is now clarified: the bracketed purpose clause is set off as an explanatory aside about their liability, not as a result of Justin's request to publish.

problems.quote: since they claim we do such things, they condemn themselves, so that they need no other judges
problems.source_quote: ὡς ἐκ τοῦ καὶ ἡμῖν, ὡς τοιαῦτα πράττουσι, θάνατον ἢ δεσμὰ ἢ ἄλλο τι τοιοῦτον προστιμᾶν ἑαυτοὺς κατακρίνειν, ὡς μὴ δέεσθαι ἄλλων δικαστῶν
problems.why: Subject flipped: source says 'by imposing... on us... they condemn themselves,' but English makes 'they' the imposers and self-condemners, obscuring that the judges' penalty on Christians becomes self-condemnation.
problems.fix: for by imposing death or imprisonment or such penalty on us, as though we did such things, they condemn themselves, needing no other judges.

problems.quote: These people become liable to punishment through their own fault—that these things may be known to all people—because
problems.source_quote: οἳ παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν αἰτίαν ὑπεύθυνοι ταῖς τιμωρίαις γίνονται [εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα], διὰ τὸ
problems.why: Bracketed phrase mispositioned: in source it explains purpose of publication, not reason for punishment.
problems.fix: They become liable to punishment through their own fault, [so that these things may be known to all people,] because
problems.ruling: εἰς τὸ γνωσθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ταῦτα belongs with publishing the book (ὅπως γνωσθῇ), not punishment; misplacement misleads reader.

last_rejected.quote: so that these things may be known to all people
last_rejected.why: Bracketed text in source is likely editorial insertion; English treats as authentic, changing syntax.
last_rejected.fix: Omit 'so that these things may be known to all people' or mark as uncertain.
last_rejected.ruling: Brackets are editorial; translator may legitimately include text. Meaning not changed by treating it as authentic.

last_rejected.why: 'shameful' for αἰσχροῦ is too narrow; context is 'ignorance of good things,' so 'base' or 'evil' better.
last_rejected.fix: ignorance of what is good and base
last_rejected.ruling: αἰσχρός commonly means 'shameful'; within normal range. Contrast with καλοῦ supports good/shameful pairing.

last_rejected.why: Final clause explains self-condemnation result; 'needing' loses the 'so that' force of ὡς μή.
last_rejected.fix: so that they need no other judges
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς μή here expresses result/extent; 'needing no other judges' captures self-condemnation adequately.
